Read survey data into an sd_data object

Source: R/read.R
sd_read.Rd

Reads a survey dataset from disk and wraps it in an sd_data object (see new_sd_data()). The file format is chosen automatically from the file extension. Currently supported: .csv, .tsv, .xlsx, .xls, .sav (SPSS), .dta (Stata), and .rds.

Usage

sd_read(path, encoding = "UTF-8", ...)

Arguments

path

Path to the data file.

encoding

Text encoding to assume for csv/tsv files. Defaults to "UTF-8". Ignored for other formats.

...

Further arguments passed on to the underlying reader function (utils::read.csv(), utils::read.delim(), readxl::read_excel(), haven::read_sav(), or haven::read_dta()).

Value

An sd_data object.

Details

When the source data carries labels of its own (SPSS .sav, Stata .dta, read via the haven package, or an .rds file containing an already-labelled data frame from an earlier session), the variable labels are copied into meta$labels and the value labels into meta$value_labels automatically – this harvesting happens inside new_sd_data() and applies to any data frame with label/labels column attributes, regardless of source format. For formats without built-in labels (csv, tsv, xlsx), these start out empty and can be filled in afterwards.

sd_read() does not itself set variable roles or missing-value codes — those are the next steps in the pipeline (sd_detect_roles() and sd_set_missing()).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aineisto <- sd_read("survey_data.csv")
aineisto <- sd_read("survey_data.sav")
} # }
